label: REAL — measured on this machine's loopback interface (127.0.0.1)
method: Sockets are real; both endpoints run in this process on 127.0.0.1 (threads).
Latency: sequential request/response round trips, timed with perf_counter, one in flight.
TCP bulk: sendall() of bulk_bytes in 64 KiB blocks, timed until the receiver's 1-byte ack.
UDP bulk: datagrams sent back to back; the receiver counts what arrives (sequence numbers).
TCP connect time is the time for connect() to return (kernel handshake).

bulk.note: Delivery is confirmed by the receiver's end-of-transfer acknowledgement.

The sender is not slowed by the receiver. Any shortfall in delivered_ratio is real datagram loss (e.g. receive-buffer overflow) observed on this machine; 1.0 means none was seen in this run, not that UDP is lossless.

findings: Median round-trip on loopback: TCP 0.0951 ms, UDP 0.0319 ms (small messages, this run only).
TCP connect() took 0.7304 ms; UDP needs no setup.
Bulk: TCP moved 46.0 Mbit/s with 100% delivery; UDP sent at 683.99 Mbit/s and 100.00% of datagrams arrived (0 reordered, 0 duplicated).
These figures describe loopback on this machine only; they do not show that either protocol is generally faster.
limitations: Loopback has no propagation delay, bandwidth limit or normal packet loss; results do not predict LAN or Internet behaviour.
Sender, receiver and the Python interpreter share one machine and one GIL; absolute numbers depend on load.
No loss or delay is injected, so this mode cannot show TCP retransmission or UDP loss under impairment — use simulated mode for that.
Single run per call; repeat to see variance.

protocol_notes.tcp: Three-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK) before any data: one extra round trip.
protocol_notes.udp: None. The first datagram carries data.

protocol_notes.tcp: Lost segments are detected (duplicate ACKs, timeouts) and retransmitted until acknowledged.
protocol_notes.udp: None. A lost datagram is gone unless the application retransmits it.

protocol_notes.tcp: A byte stream: the receiver gets bytes in order; a gap holds back later data.
protocol_notes.udp: Independent datagrams; they may arrive reordered, duplicated or not at all.

protocol_notes.tcp: Cumulative ACKs drive retransmission and the congestion window.
Reduces its sending rate when it infers congestion.
protocol_notes.udp: None built in; the sender sets its own rate.

protocol_notes.tcp: None: the stream must be framed by the application.

execution.title: TCP and UDP loopback experiment
execution.operation: Opens real TCP and UDP sockets on 127.0.0.1 and times connect, round trips and bulk transfer.
limitations: Loopback has no propagation delay, bandwidth limit or normal loss; no impairment is injected.
